props.gloss_en: once the wicked kingdom decreed that Israel should not engage in Torah
Pappos ben Yehuda came and found R' Akiva convening assemblies in public and engaging in Torah
Pappos: Akiva, are you not afraid of the kingdom?

R' Akiva's parable: a fox walking by the river told the fleeing fish to come up onto dry land and dwell with him; they said: you are no clever one but a fool -- if in the place of our life we are afraid, in the place of our death all the more so
so we, now sitting and engaging in Torah, of which it is written: 'for it is your life and the length of your days' (Deut 30:20)
they said: not many days passed before they seized R' Akiva and imprisoned him, and seized Pappos ben Yehuda and imprisoned him beside him
R' Akiva: Pappos, who brought you here?
Pappos: happy are you, R' Akiva, that you were seized over words of Torah; woe to Pappos, who was seized over idle matters
when they took R' Akiva out to be killed it was the time of the Shema; they were combing his flesh with iron combs, and he was accepting upon himself the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven
his students: our master, this far?!
R' Akiva: all my days I was troubled over this verse, 'with all your soul' -- even if He takes your soul
R' Akiva: I said, when will it come to my hand that I may fulfil it? and now that it has come to my hand, shall I not fulfil it?
he prolonged 'echad' until his soul left [him] at 'echad'
a bat kol: happy are you, R' Akiva, that your soul left at 'echad'
the ministering angels before the Holy One: this is Torah and this its reward? 'from men, by Your hand, O Lord, from men...' (Ps 17:14)
He said to them: 'their portion is in life' (Ps 17:14)
a bat kol came out and said: happy are you, R' Akiva, for you are destined for the life of the world to come
